title: Template drafts served during a provider outage use up the officer's daily AI quota
impact: When no provider answers, each click still creates an ANNOUNCEMENT_DRAFT row, and announcementGenerationQuota() counts those rows. An officer who retries during an outage burns all 20 daily drafts on identical boilerplate and gets 'Daily limit reached' once the AI is back.
suggested_fix: Count only model-written drafts in announcementGenerationQuota(), for example add ->where('model_name', '!=', 'template-draft') or ->where('context_version', 'announcement-v2'). Alternatively, do not create a quota-counted row for a template and return the template with ai_output_id null.
verifier_notes: generateDraft creates an ANNOUNCEMENT_DRAFT AiOutput row for template drafts too (model_name template-draft, context_version announcement-template-v1), and announcementGenerationQuota() counts every ANNOUNCEMENT_DRAFT row for requested_by today without filtering by model or context_version. User::getIdAttribute maps id to school_id, so the requested_by filter matches.
corrected_fix: Filter on context_version ('announcement-v2') rather than model_name, since model_name for real drafts varies by provider.

title: The deterministic fallback draft discards the officer's details, audience and category
evidence: private function fallbackAnnouncementDraft(string $prompt): string { $title = Str::after($prompt, 'Title: '); ... return "{$title}\n\nPlease be informed of this important HIUSA announcement. Kindly review the details, ..."; }
impact: The officer types facts such as 'Assembly is on September 30 at 2:00 PM. Bring your ID.' into the AI instructions box. When no provider answers, those facts are dropped and replaced with generic copy. The notice then tells them to 'Add the date, place and other details', which they already gave. The template also repeats the title as the body's first line, so a posted announcement shows its title twice, and it calls every organization's post a 'HIUSA announcement'.
suggested_fix: Build the template from $data rather than parsing $prompt: open with one line for the audience, include $data['details'] verbatim when present, and leave the title out of the body. Change the notice to say the AI writer was unavailable and the officer's notes were inserted as written.
verifier_notes: fallbackAnnouncementDraft() takes only $prompt, pulls the title out of it, and returns fixed copy that starts with the title and says "HIUSA announcement"; $data['details'], audience and category are never used. The notice tells the officer to add details they may already have typed.

title: Announcement drafts are never checked for invented dates, times, fees or numbers
impact: The instructions say 'Never invent dates, times, venues, fees ...', but nothing in the code enforces it. Every other feature gates its copy with preservesNumericFacts(); this one does not. A model-invented date, time or fee goes straight into the body field, and an Admin can publish it at once with 'Publish now'. AiLiveEval reports ungrounded numbers for this feature, but production ignores them.
suggested_fix: After plainText(), call $this->ai->preservesNumericFacts($generated['text'], [$data['title'], $data['details'] ?? '']). If it returns false, set $generated = null so the deterministic template (with the officer's details, see finding 02) is used.
verifier_notes: After generate(), only plainText() and an empty check run. preservesNumericFacts() is used by Financial report, Forecast, Event, Task, Budget and AskAi, but not here. numericValues() parses numbers inside strings, so passing title and details as facts works as the fix describes. The officer does edit the body before posting, which reduces but does not remove the risk.

title: A first-provider answer that fails the caller's validation never falls through to the second provider
impact: serve() stops at the first non-null result. Callers do their real validation afterwards: normalizeWorkflow() in EventController::generatePlan, the numeric checks on explanations, and an empty plainText() in announcement drafts. When Claude returns a schema-valid answer that fails those checks, the user gets the template, or for workflow explanations no AI note at all, even though Groq might have produced a valid answer.
suggested_fix: Add an optional validator closure to the call, for example generateStructured(..., ?callable $accept = null) or a FallbackTextGenerator::serveValidated(). serve() would then try the secondary when $accept($result) is false. Pass normalizeWorkflow and the explanation and number checks from the callers.
verifier_notes: serve() returns the first non-null result, and callers validate afterwards, so a primary answer that fails caller validation never reaches the secondary. The class docblock states this is intended ("secondary only when the primary answers nothing"), so this is a design limitation rather than a bug. The impact is lower than stated because the secondary would see the same prompt and often fail the same checks.
corrected_fix: Optional: add an accept callback to serve() and expose it through generate()/generateStructured() on FallbackTextGenerator only. Treat it as an enhancement at low severity, not a defect.

title: Fallback chain can block a web request for 24+ seconds with no circuit breaker
evidence:
$total = (float) ($seconds ?? max(1, min(self::MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS, (int) config('services.anthropic.timeout') ?: self::MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS)));  // 12s
// GroqResponsesService: ->timeout(max(1, min(self::MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS, ...)))  // another 12s
impact: During a Claude outage or slowdown, every draft, plan, advice and forecast request waits the full 12s Claude timeout, then up to 12s more for Groq, before the template is served. Nothing remembers a recent failure. The event plan asks for 2400 output tokens (3600 with TOKEN_HEADROOM) within 12s, so it is the call most likely to hit that timeout. PHP-FPM workers are tied up for the whole wait, which compounds under the ai-generation limit of 5 per minute per user.
suggested_fix: After a timeout, connection error or 5xx, set a short Cache flag (for example ai:anthropic:down for 60s) and skip that provider while it is set. Also give the two attempts one shared deadline, for example pass the remaining seconds to the secondary, so the whole chain stays under about 15s.
verifier_notes: Claude caps the total at 12s (connect_timeout 3s) with maxRetries 0, and Groq caps at 12s (connect_timeout 5s). FallbackTextGenerator runs them in sequence with no shared deadline and no memory of recent failures, so the worst case is about 24s per request.

title: Generating a draft silently overwrites announcement text the user already wrote
impact: An officer who writes part of the body and then opens 'Draft the text with AI' and clicks Generate loses their text with no warning and no undo. If output_text comes back empty, the body is cleared.
suggested_fix: If body.trim() is not empty, ask for confirmation before replacing it, using the page's existing ConfirmModal, or keep the previous body in state and offer an 'Undo' button next to the draft notice. Never set the body to '' when output_text is missing.
verifier_notes: handleGenerateDraft calls setBody(res.data?.output_text || '') with no check of the existing body and nothing to undo. The server always returns non-empty text (the template replaces empty output), so clearing to '' only happens on a malformed response.

title: Draft 'details' input has no length limit on the server or the client
impact: Any Admin or Officer can send megabytes of 'details'. The whole string goes to Claude, and then to Groq, as paid input tokens, up to 20 times a day per user. It is also stored twice in ai_outputs (prompt_text and structured_input). An oversized request fails at Claude as a 400, then at Groq, and falls back to the template only after both paid round trips.
suggested_fix: Validate 'details' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:2000'] with a clear message, and add maxLength={2000} plus a character counter to the textarea.
verifier_notes: The validation for 'details' is ['nullable','string'] with no max, and the client Textarea has no maxLength (title has 255 and body has 10000). The size is bounded in practice only by PHP post_max_size and web-server body limits, which are still far beyond what a prompt needs.

title: Configured provider timeouts above 12s are silently ignored; GROQ_TIMEOUT defaults to 25
evidence:
'timeout' => env('GROQ_TIMEOUT', 25),
// GroqResponsesService: ->timeout(max(1, min(self::MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS, (int) config('services.groq.timeout') ?: self::MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS)))  // MAX_REQUEST_SECONDS = 12
impact: The config file says Groq waits 25s, but the code caps it at 12s, and ANTHROPIC_TIMEOUT above 12 is cut the same way. An operator who raises a timeout to get long event plans through sees no change, and nothing logs the cap.
suggested_fix: Set the config default to 12. Either document the 12s ceiling next to both keys or remove the hard cap so the config value is honoured. Log a warning when a configured value is clamped.
verifier_notes: config/services.php sets GROQ_TIMEOUT to 25, but GroqResponsesService clamps it with min(12, ...). ANTHROPIC_TIMEOUT is clamped the same way. Nothing records the clamp.

title: Quota hint shows '20 of 20 drafts left today' when the quota request fails
evidence:
const [generationQuota, setGenerationQuota] = useState({ limit: 20, used: 0, remaining: 20 });
... getAnnouncementGenerationQuota().then(...).catch(() => {})
impact: If GET /announcements/generation-quota fails, or the server limit is not 20, the hint shows a made-up full quota. The Generate button stays enabled even for a user who has none left, and they only learn this from a 429 after clicking.
suggested_fix: Start generationQuota as null. Render the hint only once real data arrives, and on failure show 'Daily limit unavailable' (without the 20 of 20 count) and leave the button enabled.
verifier_notes: The initial state is {limit:20, used:0, remaining:20}, and the effect's .catch(() => {}) leaves it in place. Once quotaLoading is false, the hint shows "20 of 20", and the button is enabled on that placeholder.

title: Daily quota check and draft insert are not atomic, so concurrent requests exceed the limit
impact: The count is read before a provider call that can take up to about 24s, and the row is written afterwards. Up to five parallel requests (the ai-generation limit) all pass the same 'remaining = 1' check, so the daily limit is not a real cap on paid calls. The version computed as max('version') + 1 can also be duplicated.
suggested_fix: Reserve a slot before calling the provider: an atomic Cache::increment on a per-user, per-day key compared against the limit, or a pending AiOutput row inserted first and updated afterwards. Release the slot if the result is a template.
verifier_notes: The quota is read before generate() (up to about 24s) and AiOutput::create runs afterwards, with no lock or reservation. The ai-generation limiter allows 5 per minute, so parallel requests can all pass the same remaining check. version uses max()+1 with no lock either.

title: ai:live-eval default output folder is a Windows drive path
evidence:
{--out=D:/Claude/scratch/hiusa-ai : Folder for the eval-<feature>.json files}
... mkdir($out, 0777, true)
impact: On Linux (CI, the Lightsail host, cloud sessions), running the command without --out creates a relative directory tree 'D:/Claude/scratch/hiusa-ai' inside the current working directory, usually the repository's server folder. The eval JSON, including full prompts, then lands in an untracked folder in the checkout.
suggested_fix: Default to storage_path('app/ai-live-eval') (set it in handle() when the option is empty) and keep the Windows scratch path as a documented --out example only.
verifier_notes: The default for --out is D:/Claude/scratch/hiusa-ai, and handle() runs mkdir($out, 0777, true) on it. On Linux that creates a relative D: tree under the working directory. Impact is smaller than stated: the command refuses production and uses invented demo data, so the prompts hold no real records.
